summary: Anchored the registered propagation question's last unsourced claim and re-stated its analysis. A new source, src_compaction_trailing (snapshot.go:217-250), records that compactLogsWithTrailing deletes only up to min(snapshot index, last log index minus TrailingLogs) and says so explicitly - it ensures at least TrailingLogs entries and does not allow logs after the snapshot to be removed - so trimming cannot be the reason a joiner misses a corrective entry. The successor interpretation for dec7dd4ba25743138e52303340152c0c-question-0 combines that with the install path (the joiner's configuration, lastApplied and lastSnapshot come from the snapshot and its index, raft.go:1880-1975), the scan of entries above that index (raft.go:1595-1620) and the snapshot writer's use of the tracked committed configuration (snapshot.go:155-190), and concludes that a stale snapshot is corrected exactly when its corrective entry lies above the installed snapshot index: the persistent case is a node whose tracked committed configuration is the stale one and which snapshots again so that the corrective entry lies below the new snapshot index, which no trimming can explain away. The question stays open by observation rather than mechanism, with counterevidence noting that the account is source-read rather than observed and that a joiner's own snapshots could correct it by routes not enumerated, and with the run's two defect accounts and all their receipts unchanged. No execution is submitted, as none can be completed and cited within the allocation.
